title: Evaluating Compressibility Assumptions for Geological CO₂ Storage Using Linear and Nonlinear Compression Evidence
content: Geological CO₂ storage requires compressibility assumptions suited to the effective-stress interval and loading path. We assess their adequacy by separating curve approximation, prediction, parameter identification, and storage consequence. An exact minimax bound tests when a constant logarithmic slope cannot meet a specified tolerance. Across 19 published sediment trajectories, full-data calibration of Arc Joint via Optimum Parameters (AJOP) gave a median range-normalized void-ratio RMSE of 1.27% and a maximum of 3.41% for its five-parameter form; 12 fits selected its exact linear member. The quadratic had a lower median error but locally reversed compression in four cases. Separate blocked tests, thirteen independent Boston Blue Clay specimens, and an intact Draupne record expose limits on prediction and transfer. In twelve archived Smeaheia scenarios, compressibility choices changed pressure-screen classifications. The assessment connects tests of simple assumptions, the value of added curvature, and calibration requirements to storage screening, while preserving the distinction between successful loading-curve approximation and field validation.
